extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and writers creating/publishing mathematical content on Medium and similar online platforms
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for producing readable, professional-looking mathematics posts on Medium, covering inline notation, displayed equations as images, software and file-management practices, and typographic/retina-aware considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variables in italics
rubrics_metrics.description: Variables like *x* and *y* can simply be italicized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer using plain italic characters for simple inline variables rather than images or complicated formatting; this keeps inline math readable and integrates with surrounding text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Unicode for notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Unicode to expand notation options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unicode symbols allow more mathematical glyphs inline without images; combine with fonts and copy/paste where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX-to-Unicode browser extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX-to-Unicode browser extensions help LaTeX-trained writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Install extensions that convert LaTeX-like input to Unicode so authors comfortable with TeX can produce inline math quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use OS character picker
rubrics_metrics.description: Edit > Emoji & Symbols for Mac users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the operating system's character picker (e.g., Mac's Emoji & Symbols) to insert uncommon Unicode math symbols when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Render complex expressions as images
rubrics_metrics.description: Render complex expressions as images rather than relying on inline text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For anything more than short inline symbols (multi-line equations, complicated fractions, matrices), create images so layout and spacing remain correct across Medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep image sizes small
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep image sizes small so they display at full resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Export images at small pixel dimensions but high-resolution (use @2x technique) so Medium displays them sharply without downscaling artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use @2x filenames for retina
rubrics_metrics.description: Use `@2x` filenames to preserve retina display quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name images with @2x suffix and supply appropriately sized images so high-DPI displays show crisp math images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-image width ~300px
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-image width ~300px for proper text scaling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target ~300px width for single equation images so they integrate with text size and line-height on Medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter font, 10px x-height
rubrics_metrics.description: Charter font, 10px x-height for typography consistency with Medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a font and x-height that match Medium's body text (Charter 10px x-height recommended) so math images blend visually with surrounding text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use image grids to optimise space
rubrics_metrics.description: Use image grids (505px for 2-column, 333px for 3-column) to optimise space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange related equation images in Medium's image-grid layouts using the recommended column widths to save vertical space and maintain readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeXiT for generating images
rubrics_metrics.description: LaTeXiT for generating math expression images at 200% scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use LaTeXiT to typeset equations and export at double scale (@2x) so downsampled images remain sharp on standard and retina displays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Photoshop for image refinement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use image-editing tools (e.g., Photoshop) to crop, align, and fine-tune rendered equation images before uploading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard LaTeX with screenshots as alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard LaTeX with screenshots as alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If LaTeXiT isn't available, render in a standard LaTeX workflow and take high-resolution screenshots, then edit/export for web use.

rubrics_metrics.name: SVG + JavaScript for precise diagrams
rubrics_metrics.description: SVG + JavaScript for geometric diagrams requiring precise coordinates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For diagrams where coordinates must be exact or interactive, prefer SVG (possibly with JavaScript) rather than bitmap images to preserve precision and scalability.

rubrics_metrics.name: QuickTime + GIFBrewery for animations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture animations or dynamic demonstrations using screen recording (QuickTime) and convert/optimize to GIFs with tools like GIFBrewery for embedding.

rubrics_metrics.name: ImageOptim to shrink GIFs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ImageOptim or similar tools to reduce file size of GIFs and images so posts load quickly while preserving visual fidelity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tag images with short English phrases
rubrics_metrics.description: Tag images with short English phrases for organisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use human-readable, concise tags on image files to keep source assets organised and searchable for future edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain PSD source files
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain PSD source files for future editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep layered source files (e.g., PSDs) so images and equations can be re-exported or adjusted later without retypesetting from scratch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typography and image quality are first-class concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Online platforms impose a distinct rubric: typography + image quality + retina-aware sizing become first-class concerns alongside mathematical content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'good' Medium math piece looks polished even before it's read — visual integration, consistent typography, and properly scaled, sharp equations are as important as correctness and exposition.
